topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes for cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks introduce the lecture objectives and outline the framework for understanding cancer hallmarks and tumor progression.

topics.label: Growth signal independence and signaling pathway deregulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in growth factor and receptor signaling cascades enable cancer cells to achieve growth signal autonomy and evade inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation in tumor development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how differentiation blocks prevent cells from reaching mature functional states and sustain proliferation in hematopoietic and epithelial tissues.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis via p53 and Bcl-2 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how cancer cells avoid programmed cell death through p53 disruption and altered balances of pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, telomere maintenance, and senescence bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells overcome the Hayflick limit and bypass stress-induced senescence checkpoints through telomerase reactivation and p53 evasion.

topics.label: Complex hallmarks and cancer metabolic rewiring
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce complex cancer hallmarks and examine how aerobic glycolysis, metabolic rewiring, and oncometabolites drive tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis and vascularization
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how tumors trigger new blood vessel formation to overcome hypoxia and supply growing tissue with essential nutrients.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dissemination, and genetics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the multistep metastatic cascade, monitoring via circulating tumor cells, metastatic inefficiency, and genomic alterations in secondary tumors.

topics.label: Summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: These closing remarks summarize the collective nature of cancer hallmarks and conclude the lecture.
